competences: The learner describes practical ways Christians cooperate in their communities.
The learner names Christian organisations and explains how they care for people in need.
languageCompetence: Read, pronounce and spell cooperation, volunteer, leadership, community, charity and welfare.
objectives: By the end of the lesson learners should identify at least five methods of cooperation.
By the end of the lesson learners should name three organisations which help communities and state their work.
priorKnowledge: Learners have studied the meaning and value of working together, including Christian examples of unselfishness.
materials: Chart listing local Christian voluntary organisations
Primary Six CRE source notes about cooperative service
references: P.6 C.R.E TERM III LESSON NOTES, 2022

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the benefits of working together studied earlier and asks "6. State any two organization that help people in need". They introduce cooperation as practical service and care for community members.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the importance of teamwork, answer the original question and name a way Christians help other people.

steps.content: Cooperation means working together to reach a desired goal. Christians cooperate when they work towards common objectives. Cooperation helps people overcome common problems. Working together encourages people to support each other.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents and writes the sourced points for "Meaning of cooperation", beginning with "Cooperation means working together to reach a desired goal. Christians cooperate when they work towards common objectives." They check learners' understanding using the exact question "6. State any two organization that help people in need" and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the teaching points, identify forms of Christian service and copy the sourced notes into their books.

steps.content: By working together as a team. By practising good and open leadership. By supporting democratic laws and rules. By showing concern for the welfare of others. By working hard towards a shared goal. By providing peace, freedom and security. By caring properly for God's creation. By allowing people to share useful ideas.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents and writes the sourced points for "Ways of cooperation", beginning with "By working together as a team. By practising good and open leadership." They check learners' understanding using the exact question "Why do we need Christian voluntary organization?" and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the teaching points, identify forms of Christian service and copy the sourced notes into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Examples of Christian voluntary organisations
steps.content: The Young Women's Christian Association serves people. The Bible Society spreads the word of God. World Vision International builds and facilitates schools. The Mother's Union helps people in communities. The Christian Children's Fund supports needy children. The Adventist Development Relief Agency helps communities. Scripture Union promotes teaching the word of God.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents and writes the sourced points for "Examples of Christian voluntary organisations", beginning with "The Young Women's Christian Association serves people. The Bible Society spreads the word of God." They check learners' understanding using the exact question "Mention any two Christian organization which help women only" and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the teaching points, identify forms of Christian service and copy the sourced notes into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Ways Christians care for others
steps.content: By providing food to people who are hungry. By helping those who are weak. By being generous to other people. By caring for people who are sick. By offering support to people in sorrow. By acting fairly towards other people. By sharing needed resources with others.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents and writes the sourced points for "Ways Christians care for others", beginning with "By providing food to people who are hungry. By helping those who are weak." They check learners' understanding using the exact question "How can one use his/ her talents to benefit the world?" and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the teaching points, identify forms of Christian service and copy the sourced notes into their books.

steps.content: 6. State any two organization that help people in need | Why do we need Christian voluntary organization? | Mention any two Christian organization which help women only | How can one use his/ her talents to benefit the world? | 1. What are voluntary organizations?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the five sourced questions, beginning with "6. State any two organization that help people in need" and "Why do we need Christian voluntary organization?". They supervise the class, mark original answers and correct misunderstandings using the reference texts.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the written questions independently, identify Christian organisations, and correct responses after receiving the teacher's feedback.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews forms of teamwork and voluntary service, then checks knowledge using "Mention any two Christian organization which help women only" and "How can one use his/ her talents to benefit the world?". They assign the final source question as homework.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give examples of cooperation and explain one form of Christian service before recording their homework.

assessment: Ask "6. State any two organization that help people in need", "Why do we need Christian voluntary organization?", and "Mention any two Christian organization which help women only". Mark written answers using the cited source passages and explain any errors.
homework: Answer the sourced question "1. What are voluntary organizations?"
